export const meta = {
  name: 'aa4-explore',
  description: 'Two AA4 explorers chase reference-quality waterline edges: GBAA contour distance vs MLAA on the exact lake mask',
  phases: [{ title: 'Explore', detail: 'two angles, own lanes and labs' }],
}

const X = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    angle: { type: 'string' },
    implemented: { type: 'boolean' },
    switch: { type: 'string' },
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    replaces_C: { type: 'boolean' },
    metrics_table: { type: 'string', description: 'per path: BASE / AA3 / yours / GT for edge error vs GT, MCE, MC32, J48, J32, texture, flash peak' },
    edge_error_reduction_vs_base: { type: 'string' },
    perf_vs_base: { type: 'string' },
    gates: {
      type: 'array',
      items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string' }, numbers: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'verdict'] },
    },
    slices: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    patch_path: { type: 'string' },
    log_path: { type: 'string' },
    recommendation: { type: 'string', enum: ['adopt', 'adopt-with-fixes', 'reject'] },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['angle', 'implemented', 'metrics_table', 'recommendation', 'patch_path', 'log_path'],
}

phase('Explore')
const res = await parallel(args.explorers.map((x) => () =>
  agent(`${args.common}\n\n${args.explore}\n\n${x.prompt}`, { label: `explore:${x.key}`, phase: 'Explore', schema: X })))
const out = res.map((r, i) => (r ? { ...r, key: args.explorers[i].key } : null))
if (out.some((r) => !r)) log('an explorer returned nothing')
return out

CONTEXT - Retrux hero, waterline anti-aliasing (20 Nov 2026, Asia/Jakarta time).
The site is a real-time three.js r184 / WebGL2 hero: ice rings above a mirror lake among snow, rocks, ice slabs and floes. Quality tiers: T0 phones / iGPU (FXAA, plate lake, DPR 1), T1 desktop (MSAA 4, mirror lake LAKE_R12), T2 (MSAA 4, higher). The user's words: "benerin pinggiran air di deket es itu kalo geser kamera kek low quality anti aliasing gitu, tapi dia aneh glitch gitu, make it smooth yaa" (the water edge near the ice looks like low-quality anti-aliasing when the camera moves, with a weird glitch; make it smooth) and today "priority benerin anti aliasing water yaa, ensure everything perfect". House rules: the user's words win; build nothing beyond the brief; look at your own images with the Read tool (zoomed crops, time slices, strips), never judge by numbers alone; report failures honestly.

  C  lake-edge TAA pass inside EnvEdge on the waterline band only (pixels whose 3x3 + 4 far taps hold lake AND solid, classified from the alpha view distance vs the analytic lake-plane distance), weight 0.5, Catmull-Rom history clamped to its 2x2 footprint, variance box intersected with the 3x3 min/max as the clip, in the compressed space; no history near the hero reflection or in the hold's crest reach; skipped after 24 frames of still camera (switch ?lktaa=0; lab-only params need ?debug: lktaaw, lktaacrest=0, lktaa=1 on the plate lake)

  G4 no outlines / halos: no pixel more than 4 levels outside the no-AA 3x3 neighbourhood range in motion.
  G5 hero (rings, orb, shards), clouds, mist, sky unchanged; no seams.
  G6 flash gone (no periodic component along the waterline in motion).
  G7 frame time at T1 <= +5 % of BASE while moving (interleaved A/B, scale pinned).
  G8 your switch off == AA3 exactly; all switches off == BASE; T0 and ?envlake=plate unchanged by default (you may improve T0 / plate lake only behind a switch, never regress).

args.explore:
ROLE: AA4 EXPLORER (builder). Goal: waterline edges that glide like the 16-sample GT while the camera moves (G1b), with every other gate at least as good as AA3 and the total cost <= +5 % of BASE at T1 while moving. AA3 already costs +4.5..+5.9 %, so your method may replace C (the TAA pass) if it subsumes it; keep B (it removes the flash) unless you prove an equal fix that is cheaper.
Work only in your own lane (an APFS clone of the AA3 lane, yours alone) with your own lab port; use the BASE lab :5182 read-only for BASE / GT captures; reuse the GT caps (re-render more GT from :5182 with the builder's recipe if you need other paths). Your change gets its own URL switch that restores AA3 exactly (prove it with ident / g8-style checks). Mirror your patch (diff vs aa3_judged) and a dated LOG into your MAIN backup folder after every sub-step.
Method: first understand how the waterline is drawn (world/Water.ts, world/LakeMirror.ts, world/LakeSchedule.ts, world/PlateEnvironment.ts and the baked environment materials, world/EnvEdge.ts, the AA_RESOLVE chunk in shaders/chunks.ts, any SHORE_AA on T0); prototype offline when it helps; implement; measure with crawl.mjs plus an edge-only error vs GT that you add; make BASE | AA3 | yours | GT slices for all six boxes and open them; iterate. Time box 150 min. Report honestly: a well-measured failure is a useful result.

explorers.prompt:
ANGLE X1 - geometry-buffer AA (GBAA-style) for the waterline. Your lane: /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa4x/retrux-web ; your lab port 5191 ; work folder SP/work4/aa4x ; backup folder MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa4x/ ; switch ?gbaa=0.
Idea: the waterline is the contour where a solid surface crosses the analytic lake plane. A solid fragment knows its height above the plane h and the screen-space gradient of h (dFdx / dFdy), so the signed distance from the pixel centre to the contour, in pixels, is about h / |grad h| (the water side can derive the same from the plane and its neighbours' view distance). Get that distance (and the edge orientation) to the EnvEdge pass (which already reads the resolved image whose alpha carries view distance), and there give each pixel within about 1 px of the contour a continuous coverage, blending with the neighbour across the contour: sub-pixel exact and temporally stable by construction. Watch: the MSAA resolve averages any channel across the edge; the tone-compressed resolve; solids' contours also appear in the mirror reflection; far floes where the gradient is tiny; slab feet under ripples; the hold's crest train; the hero reflection.

ANGLE X2 - morphological AA on the exact geometric lake / solid mask (MLAA / SMAA-style, no new shader outputs). Your lane: /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa4y/retrux-web ; your lab port 5192 ; work folder SP/work4/aa4y ; backup folder MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa4y/ ; switch ?lkmlaa=0.
Idea: AA3's band classification (alpha view distance vs the analytic lake-plane distance) already gives an exact per-pixel lake / solid mask. Waterlines are long, mostly near-horizontal contours - exactly the case where MLAA / SMAA edge-length search reconstructs the true line best. Detect the mask's edges, search edge lengths and crossing ends, compute sub-pixel coverage areas, and blend each pixel with its neighbour across the edge (in the resolve's compressed space, as C does), so the edge position becomes continuous and glides with the camera. Watch: double AA with the MSAA resolve (edge pixels are already partly mixed); short edges and corners at rock clusters; far floes 1-2 px tall; temporal stability of the search; how it combines with C (keep, replace or blend).

result.angle: X1: geometry-buffer AA (GBAA) for the waterline. Final default build is X7. A contact-line fit uses the solid's height above the analytic lake plane, rebuilt from the half-float alpha distance; for silhouettes, a straight-edge Gauss-Newton fit runs on the 4x coverage of a 5x5 window. Both are applied inside AA3's TAA pass to the current frame before the history blend. Switch: ?gbaa=0.
result.edge_error_reduction_vs_base: None. On edge pixels, error vs the 16-sample GT went from 4.717 to 4.736 on medium (+0.4%; AA3 -0.8%) and from 4.463 to 4.520 on slow (+1.3%; AA3 +0.4%). RMS luma is -10% medium and -9% slow, against AA3's -11% and -9%. The best intermediate versions (X5, X6) reached -3% on the mean, but their RMS and crawl were worse than AA3. The -40% target is out of reach as defined: about 3.0-3.15 of the 4.7 levels is a floor that edge AA cannot remove. It comes from non-edge differences in GT's 2x render (lake texture is 0.68 of BASE, finer mirror). Removing it would mean smoothing the texture, which G3 forbids.
result.perf_vs_base: No reliable G7 number. The judges were running perf jobs at the same time, so the machine was noisy. Interleaved perf.mjs, 3 pairs, medium path, 180 frames, wall time (median of per-session medians): X7 25.42 ms, AA3 (?gbaa=0) 24.75 ms, BASE 22.46 ms. Pair ratios against BASE were 1.245 / 1.115 / 1.112 for X7 and 1.192 / 1.151 / 0.970 for AA3. AA3 itself came out at 1.15 here, against 1.059 in its builder's quiet run. X7 adds 25-tap fits on band pixels and keeps the TAA pass running at rest (history weight 0), so it can only cost more than AA3.
result.switch: ?gbaa=0 restores AA3 exactly. The GBAA shader blocks are stripped from the source unless enabled, so the off state is byte-identical to aa3_judged. Lab-only switches (need ?debug): ?gbaa=1 turns it on for the plate lake, and ?gbaadbg=1 tints changed pixels (magenta for the contact fit, yellow for the silhouette fit).

gates.verdict: pass, inherited from AA3's C; GBAA adds nothing
gates.numbers: MC32 vs BASE: slow -69% (AA3 -68%), medium -64% (AA3 -63%), fast -55% (AA3 -54%). J48 slow -58% (GT -60%), medium -20% (GT -20%). J32 slow -32% (GT -29%), medium -9% (GT -11%).

Edge error vs GT: medium +0%, slow +1% (target -40%). MCE medium -13% vs GT -21%; slow -13% vs GT -23% (both same as AA3). BASE | AA3 | X6 | X7 | GT slices: X7 looks like AA3 and still steps where GT glides (FS row 690, FF, RS, DR).

gates.verdict: pass on what was tested; partial coverage
gates.numbers: Fast-path FS strip (frames 40-64): no trail, same as AA3. The GBAA is per frame and runs before the TAA clamp. X5 showed frame-to-frame switching stipple, fixed with soft weights in X6/X7. Hold, tab hide, mid-motion resize and render-scale paths were not captured separately.
Lake 0.999-1.000, solid 1.001-1.002 of BASE on slow, medium and fast; identical to AA3.
More than 4 levels outside BASE's 3x3: medium 1047 vs AA3 1049 per Mpx; fast 1829 vs 1832. The GBAA output is clamped to the current frame's raw 3x3.

gates.verdict: inconclusive; probably at or above AA3
gates.numbers: X7 25.42 / AA3 24.75 / BASE 22.46 ms wall, noisy shared machine. Extra fits on band pixels, plus the TAA pass now also runs at rest.

?gbaa=0 vs the AA3 lane ident: final image, mirror, walk, cache, cacheN and reflection targets and all 15 program sources identical. ?gbaa=0 medium, 121 frames: 0 px differ from AA3's final caps. All switches off vs BASE T1: identical (14 programs). Plate lake, T0 and T2-off match BASE.
T0 ident identical to BASE (no EnvEdge on T0).

tsc (hero + project) clean. 0 console errors or warnings in all sessions. DPR 1 and 1.25 (dsf 2), resize 1100x700 and 1375x875 and back: no dark frame. Live engine 60 fps, TAA ran 830 frames. The patch applies to a fresh aa3_judged copy and reproduces the lane exactly.

Every slow_* slice and the X2-X7 medium slices: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-muhamadrifaldi-Documents-GitHub-retrux-hero-rnd/a0f5735b-9a7f-477e-9b57-6de40ca5644b/scratchpad/work4/aa4x/look/slices/
open_issues: Why X1 cannot meet G1b: the brief's contour h=0 is exact (fit residuals of a few hundredths of a pixel), but on a contact line the solid meets its own reflection, so the contrast is low and little changes. The visible crawl is on silhouettes, where the lake lies behind the solid, and its sub-pixel position is not in the G-buffer (alpha is the MSAA-averaged view distance).

The silhouette line fit on a 5x5 of 4x coverage matches GT quality on synthetic straight edges: coverage error 0.030 vs the 16-sample reference's 0.027 and raw 4x's 0.076 (tools/linesim*.mjs). On the real curved, cornered and textured outlines it is no more accurate than 4x plus AA3's TAA. Example: (321,711) at k100 has 4x and GT both at 157, while the fit gives 106-111.

True per-fragment GBAA for silhouettes would need triangle-edge and adjacency data, plus an extra output channel (MRT on the 4x main target) or a second geometry pass (43 draws, 225k triangles). Not attempted: it does not fit the time box or the +5% budget.

Finding for anyone rebuilding geometry from alpha: this M4 / ANGLE-Metal GPU truncates when it writes the RGBA16F target, so the stored distance can be up to 1 ulp below the true one. Measured on the open lake: h/ulp is a sawtooth from 0 to 1, always positive. My first noise model misclassified lake pixels because of this; AA3's 0.4% + 3 cm tolerance covers it.

Pre-existing in AA3, unchanged by X7: on the slow path, ALL boxes show a 1/2-cycle (30 Hz) spectral peak of 5.5x the median, against 3.9x in BASE (FF 1.7x vs 0.7x). The AA3 judges may want to check it.
G7 has no clean number because the machine was shared with the judges' perf runs. G2 hold, tab-hidden and mid-motion resize paths, and G5 hero diffs, were not captured separately for X7.
If kept for the record, X7 makes AA3's TAA pass run at rest (history weight 0) so the GBAA'd frame does not pop at the hand-over. That is a small cost at rest that AA3 does not have.

result.angle: X2: MLAA/SMAA-style morphological AA on AA3's geometric lake/solid mask. The mask comes from alpha (view distance) against the analytic lake-plane distance, and each edge pixel's coverage is rebuilt from the edge-length search. It runs inside AA3's lake-edge TAA pass (EnvEdge), in the compressed resolve space. Lane: ~/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa4y, lab :5192 (now stopped).

E2 = same with a binary mask (lake = bit0, solid = not bit0); the cap masks mark dark solids next to the lake as 'partial' because of bloom.

WHERE MLAA CHANGES PIXELS (>2 levels): only 15-31% of the changes move toward the GT, and the error on those pixels grows 1.7-3x. This holds for every variant on both paths: default, colour coverage, Z shapes only with runs of 6 px or more, with or without the TAA history. Even a perfect edge AA would reach only about -39% on E2, so the -40% target sits at this GT's theoretical limit.

open_issues: Why MLAA fails here: a 4x MSAA resolve already measures each edge pixel's coverage, including real sub-pixel shape. MLAA replaces that with a straight-line guess between mask steps plus a colour model taken from pixels 1-2 px away. On rock bumps, floe corners and curved slab feet the guess is wrong (example: medium k61 x356 y700, rock top vs lake: AA3 ~ GT, MLAA flattens the bump).

G1b (-40% edge error vs GT) looks unreachable for any edge AA with this GT. Lake-side edge pixels carry the GT's lake-texture difference (floor 6.8 levels; GT lake texture is 0.68 of BASE). A perfect edge AA would reach about -39% on E2. The lead may want to redefine the gate (solid-side pixels only, or a GT rendered with the 1x lake).

EnvEdge's silhouette blur is sigma 0.6 px at 1x, but the GT (2x render) has an effective 0.3 px. Halving it alone gives E1 -12% vs BASE and moves 56-72% of changed pixels toward GT, but crawl gets slightly worse (MC32 -59% vs -61%, MCE -11% vs -12%). A GT-like edge needs the narrower blur plus more temporal samples, which is a question for C, not X2.

Far floes (FF, medium k52-200, x 190-250, y 499-506): BASE and AA3 show a pale block under the near floe where the GT shows the floe's dark reflection (mean luma 183 vs 166; single pixels up to 70 levels off). Its edge sweeps across pixels (x230 k51->52: 117/148/160 -> 201/190/191). This is a lake-reflection difference between 1x and 2x, not edge AA, and could be part of the user's 'weird glitch'. Reported only.

The cap.mjs masks are bloom-polluted: the flat-white lake at HDR 8 blooms onto nearby solids, so dark slab faces and the far floes' dark side faces read as 'partial'. Crawl's band and the literal edge set (E1) therefore misjudge most dark waterlines. A mask session with a non-blooming flat value (e.g. 0 vs 0.5) would fix it.

A depth-based crease reconstruction (sub-pixel waterline from where lake distance minus alpha crosses zero) was checked on paper and dropped. The camera sits at 2.6 m with 0.58 mrad per pixel. At 8 m the lake distance changes 1.4 cm per row while the half-float alpha step is 0.8 cm (AA3's own tolerance there is 4.6 rows). At 35 m it gives about 0.11 px, no better than MSAA's 1/8 px.
Not run (method rejected): fast / diag / reverse / leave / hold paths, G2 ghosting cases, DPR 2 / resize / tab-visibility checks, and an interleaved G7 run against BASE on an idle machine.
My lane keeps MLAA on by default so the judged method is visible; ?lkmlaa=0 equals AA3. Do not apply aa4y.patch.
